{
  "question_intent": "Inquire about the impact of Motor Finance on other product segments and the bank's acquisition strategy in light of £30bn deployment.",
  "main_topics": ["Motor Finance impact", "Acquisition strategy", "£30bn deployment"],
  "answer_completeness": "Partial",
  "response_stance": "Deflecting",
  "evidence_level": "High",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Partially aligned",
  "question_quote": "If I think about all the products that a bank offers maybe one that has a similar structure in terms of you go to a shop, you buy something and then maybe a bank finance is offered to you without you knowing that they are acting as a corporate broker. It may be partner finance things, it may be furniture, that sort of thing. I'm not asking for you to quantify the impact, but can you sort of just help us a little bit with how those businesses work and in terms of the way the product is sold to a customer, is there any similarity between that?",
  "answer_quote": "Perlie sorry to disappoint but I'm really not going to comment further on Motor Finance. As you can imagine, we're being really thoughtful doing a lot of work in the background and when we're ready to discuss it more fully then we will obviously do so with the market. On the £30bn, I would take you back to slide 14 from our Q3 results. Our expectation was that we wouldn't see significant organic growth this year, but we did want to see a pick-up in growth, which is clearly what we've seen across Cards, Mortgages and obviously more lagged but into our Corporate Banking and Business Banking business. data.question_intent: Inquire about the impact of Motor Finance on other product segments and the bank's acquisition strategy in light of £30bn deployment.
data.question_quote: If I think about all the products that a bank offers maybe one that has a similar structure in terms of you go to a shop, you buy something and then maybe a bank finance is offered to you without you knowing that they are acting as a corporate broker. It may be partner finance things, it may be furniture, that sort of thing. I'm not asking for you to quantify the impact, but can you sort of just help us a little bit with how those businesses work and in terms of the way the product is sold to a customer, is there any similarity between that?
data.answer_quote: Perlie sorry to disappoint but I'm really not going to comment further on Motor Finance. As you can imagine, we're being really thoughtful doing a lot of work in the background and when we're ready to discuss it more fully then we will obviously do so with the market. On the £30bn, I would take you back to slide 14 from our Q3 results. Our expectation was that we wouldn't see significant organic growth this year, but we did want to see a pick-up in growth, which is clearly what we've seen across Cards, Mortgages and obviously more lagged but into our Corporate Banking and Business Banking business. As we reflect on inorganic opportunities, I would say that our plan is an organic one.
data.reason: The answer partially addresses the impact of Motor Finance on other segments and the bank's acquisition strategy, but deflects further discussion on Motor Finance and acquisition plans.
